utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Would the witness -- would the witness make the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Uscumlic. Please take a seat and make yourself comfortable.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Uscumlic, do you hear me in your language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Excellencies. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Uscumlic.

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I am waiting for the interpretation, and I do kindly ask you to wait for the transcript to stop.

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you give a statement to the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up in e-court 1D07911.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the statement you gave and signed?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does the statement accurately reflect your words?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I were to put the same questions to you today, would your answers essentially be the same?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the statement be admitted into evidence, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3552, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Since the statement itself is concise, I will not be reading the summary. Rather, I will be reading the statement, and I will then put several additional questions arising from the proofing that we had. I will read it out in English, because that's the only version there is. [In English] Witness Statement of Petar Uscumlic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether there's a point of reading entire statement instead of giving a summary. Why don't you then lead the evidence? Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: The point is so that the public can be informed of his -- of his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But it should be given in the form of a summary on the part of the accused. Reading out "I was born on the 18th," I don't see the point. Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I just may say, I agree, and if you look at the 92 per package which they filed, they do have a short summary of the statement already written in that. It's only a couple sentences and I don't know why that doesn't suffice.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, with your permission, perhaps I can make a short summary. Dr. Karadzic doesn't have that document in front of him, but if it's okay with you, I could just make a short summary of the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I have no difficulty with it, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Petar Uscumlic was working in July of 1995 as an external interpreter for the United Nations military observers stationed in Srebrenica, and he attended the meetings at the Hotel Fontana among General Mladic, the Dutch Battalion, and civilian representatives of the Muslims from Srebrenica and interpreted for the Dutch Battalion. Mr. Uscumlic was advised of testimony of Momir Nikolic concerning a conversation that allegedly occurred outside of the Fontana Hotel prior to the meeting on the morning of the 12th of July, 1995, and Mr. Uscumlic has indicated that he never heard anyone indicate that the men from Srebrenica were to be killed and had no knowledge that the prisoners would be killed. And that concludes the summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Robinson. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Uscumlic, when was it that you were in Potocari in those critical days?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I think that I was in Potocari since the 10th, and then the 11th, the 12th, and the 13th as well. I think that I was in Potocari on all these days, at least for a period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In what occasions and with whom did you spend time? In whose company were you?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: There were several occasions there. There were several messages that I had to take to the Yellow Bridge along the separation line in Potocari. When meetings were scheduled, I think that I came to the Yellow Bridge, the separation line, to receive the civilian representatives, and I then went to the meeting in Bratunac together with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I -- when the evacuation started, I was also there in front of the gate of the DutchBat compound on the 12th and the 13th. So there were several different situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In whose service for the most part? Pursuant to whose task were you present there on those days?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I was there at the disposal of everyone who needed interpretation. If the Serb side asked for a message to be taken across or for a conversation to be interpreted, I did as much. If the Dutch, and I mean the Dutch Battalion, wanted to divulge some information, at any rate, I was there to take messages across, and I was there for anyone who wanted to use my services. Formally speaking, I was employed by the UNMO, the military observers team of the United Nations which was also present there in the DutchBat Compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During these times that you spent in Potocari, did you observe any sort of mistreatment meted out by anyone?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Do you mean during the evacuation of the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I did not personally witness any major incident or any physical tussle, any threats, any weapons being drawn or anything like that. The situation was pretty chaotic, but the evacuation itself seemed to be taking its course. There were representatives of different units of the VRS present, and they directed the population toward the buses. Everything seemed to be unfolding without any use of [Realtime transcript read in error "usual"] violence or at least none that I would witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you observe the separation of the able-bodied persons from the other civilians?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In line 21, it says any "usual violence." I think the witness said "any use of violence."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm going to object now and put Mr. Karadzic on notice to leading. He said, "Did you observe the separation of able-bodied persons from other civilians?" He can just ask what did he observe, did he see any separations, and then who was separated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Mr. Uscumlic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think I said "usual violence" in Serbian. I don't know how it ended up in the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. It's noted. Before Mr. Karadzic continues, could you tell us from when you worked as an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From March 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was situated in the -- or accommodated in the Hotel Fontana in Bratunac, and the representatives of the DutchBat or UNMOs would normally come to the Yellow Bridge or to Bratunac itself, and we would proceed from there. We would either do a meeting or would travel to Belgrade, to the airport, depending on what needed to be done. As for the enclave, of course, I could not stay within the enclave at the time. At -- however, there was this one occasion when I was even driven through Srebrenica in 1994. It was right at the beginning of my service there as an interpreter. On that occasion, I had an opportunity to see what the enclave looked like within, although normally I did not enter the enclave. I was an external interpreter for the contacts with the Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: External interpreter. By external interpreter, did you mean that you were not hired or employed by either UNMO or DutchBat on a permanent basis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I mean physically external, because I was outside of the enclave. [In English] So that makes me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So to speak --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That makes me external.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You were a freelance interpreter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My contract was no different from that of other interpreters. I was employed under the same conditions as they were, the only difference being that I wasn't able to be within the enclave at the time. So I was outside. That was the difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who -- thank you. And who interpreted for them within the enclave? Were there any interpreters there?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Well, the UNMO team had two interpreters in the enclave, and the Dutch men had their own interpreters. I don't know how many and how they used them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, based on what you were able to see on the 12th and the 13th of July in Potocari, including the separation of the able-bodied, did you observe any signs? Did anything alert you to the fact that any of them would be killed? Were the actions taken there at the time alarming, in your view?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: The general situation was not your usual one, something that you would witness or experience every day. The situation could have developed into anything, really, but I didn't see at the time any signs that this would have a fateful ending for the people who were being separated. I could not have drawn such a pessimistic conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Uscumlic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions for this witness at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Uscumlic, as you have noted, your evidence in chief has been admitted in most part in written form, i.e., through your witness statement, and now you'll be cross-examined by the representative of the Office of the Prosecutor. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I actually initially had no questions for this witness, but based on the proofing note last afternoon, I will have a few.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sir, you just answered some questions, and we'll get to it in a minute, that you had no inkling that something bad would happen to these men who were separated, but something bad happened, didn't it? They were removed and murdered, and you know that; correct? As you sit here today, you know that; right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. I realise that it happened at the end. I just said that on that day, at that point in time, I could not make a conclusive inference that this would happen. I didn't have the indications of that sort. Today, at this time, of course, I'm aware that it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. I only have a few questions. First of all, do you remember you were interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor, by Mr. Jean-Rene Ruez, in July 2000?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And he thanked you at the end of that interview for coming and speaking with him?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think that he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you told the truth during that interview, didn't you, to the best of your ability?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, to the best of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And let me just say if you -- with the leave of the Chamber, of course, but if you prefer to speak English, which may feel more natural to you based on your current situation, I don't think that's a problem. Now, on the 12th of July, you've already said you were in Potocari. That was after the third Hotel Fontana meeting; right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And one thing you talk about in your interview, which is 65 ter 25074, and I'm now talking about pages 35 and 36 in e-court, is that when you got to Potocari and you saw the people there -- excuse me, this is on page 34, you said you were stunned by the number of civilians. It was a lake of people. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were very many people, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, at this time, General Mladic - you talk about this on page 35 - addressed the crowd, the lake of people, and in your words he said -- you said: "He promised them that they would be safe."

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Generally. Yes. That was something along these lines that he said in front of these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And that's at e-court page 36, actually. And he said that they would be transported on buses, and this is when you say -- you described some of the people you saw. That's on e-court page 36. You said the following describing the women you saw getting ready to go on the buses --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could Mr. Nicholls speak closer to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: "They all looked very miserable. They looked very poor, even the young women. They were teethless. They probably gave birth and during the pregnancy they didn't have enough vitamins and minerals. That was a sad sight. They looked miserable. But when the chain would let them go, a certain number that was -- that was sufficient for that convoy, that was basically the process." Were you telling the truth there when you talked about those miserable, sad, young women getting on the buses?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think that the description accurately reflects my words to Mr. Ruez. As I said, in the course of 1994, I had the rare opportunity of entering the enclave and passing through the town and see the conditions people were living in, so that the 12th of July was not the beginning of their suffering. They had gone through an ordeal and a great deal of suffering through their very presence in the enclave. And had they had an opportunity to leave the enclave and go elsewhere where they would have better living conditions, they would have done so earlier. So the 12th of July was basically the finale of a drama that they had been experiencing over the course of several years, and the several years an impact on these people.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the last sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Uscumlic, could you repeat the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that the several years of stay within the enclave had an impact on these people, the women there, and it seems that the impact was a significant one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I -- "visible" is not the same as "significant."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would rather say "obvious."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Obvious or not subtle.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now -- and you also describe, this is again at page -- now at 37 of your statement, immediately following on, you said: "On several occasions I saw that some men were preventing," I think you meant prevented, "on boarding buses and they were directed to some other directions in a couple of nearby houses and they were kept there." And that's true as well. You said that on your direct. You saw men being prevented from boarding the buses and being put in a couple of houses.

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. It happened -- or it was happening across from the gate of the DutchBat compound. So I'm probably not the only the witness who speak about it here. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And that's correct that you're not only witness, sir. Thank you. Now, just moving on to the next day, the 13th of July, and you talk about this on e-court page 45 of your statement, and I just want to confirm this, you say: "The next morning everything repeated. I also went to Potocari, and they already had one convoy that was formed," et cetera. "So the story repeated the next day with, of course, I have to notice that some adult men were separated and kept in two neighbouring houses. Later on that day, I saw a bus, I think parked there, and I think the bus picked them up and took them away." And when you describe there when you saw on the 13th to Mr. Ruez, that's true as well, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I just want to talk about these men a little bit. Mr. Karadzic was very careful, even over my objection, to again describe them as able-bodied, and certainly some of them likely were, but I want to show you what you said about some of these men that you saw. This is on page 46. You're talking about a row of houses near the power substation, and you said: "I remember one house. There were some old people there," talking about the men separated, "I really didn't know at that time why anybody would bother with them there. They looked very old. They didn't look dangerous at all." That description that you gave is also truthful, isn't?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. That description is a description of the people that I saw in that house at that time. They were really elderly people, but there would have been people of a different age too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And just to be clear, we're talking about people in this house. These are men who were separated, not allowed to board buses; right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And let me just talk about how you describe the separations. This is on your -- page 47, when you were asked about the situation and how these were taking place. You said: "A couple I noticed," and here you were talking about VRS soldiers, "that they were rude, saying some bad words, but that was all in front of the gate. We could have expected something like that, but nobody harassed anybody physically. Nobody assaulted anybody in front of my eyes except this separation. But this was also done in a quiet way without raising too much noise." So at that time, at least, when you had your interview in 2000, five years after these events, you said you didn't see any assaults except for the separations; right? You viewed those as a kind of assault.

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Well, I think that I repeated that statement when Mr. Karadzic was examining me, so I don't see a difference really. There was no physical violence. People were directed where they should go, to which buses, and that was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, I want to move on and talk about what happened after General Mladic said to the lake of people that they would be safe. This is at e-court pages 50 to 51. You knew members of the Nuhanovic family and Hasan Nuhanovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you describe in your statement being in the compound after the meetings and how the Nuhanovic family was, in your words, very frightened because Hasan's brother wasn't going to be allowed out in a convoy. Do you remember the family being frightened about their fate?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you said in your statement: "I was trying to comfort them because I just couldn't imagine that people who were registered on the lists of ICRC and UNHCR and UNPROFOR, that something bad might happen to them." Do you remember saying that in your interview? You thought they'd be okay because they were on lists.

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: But it turned out that for Ibro Nuhanovic and his son, they weren't okay, were they, once they left the compound and were separated? You talk about that in your statement too. Let me remind you what you said.

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You said -- you said at page 51, talking about Ibro Nuhanovic and his son: "Later it turned out that these people just disappeared. They showed up nowhere for exchange, for anything. I kept -- later I kept buying newspapers to see if any exchange was made for some Serbs who were held. Nothing was going on." And that's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Those are my words from my statement. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The Nuhanovics disappeared. They were murdered.

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have any re-examination, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Uscumlic, on page 13 you said that there were also people of other ages. Did you mean the people in the -- in nearby houses as well when Mr. Nicholls asked you?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I didn't go about these houses much. Basically I only saw the one facing the main street. So I cannot say if there were any other people. I think it was being said that there were a number of houses in a row, but I only saw the one closest to the main street at that time. When I say that there were other adults but of other ages, I meant -- I was speaking generally, referring also to the civilians in the DutchBat compound, but also the ones in the Srebrenica Prevoz compound. That was immediately next to the DutchBat compound. I wasn't referring to houses specifically, because I didn't go there much, and I wasn't paying much attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the last question of Mr. Nicholls, in line 9, he said that the Nuhanovics disappeared, and then they were murdered, and you answered yes. Do you have any direct knowledge about that or is that your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: PETAR USCUMLIC
utterances.text: No, of course, I don't have direct knowledge about that, but that's a logical conclusion.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Uscumlic. No more questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls, when this witness was interviewed by Mr. Ruez, was he asked about the words that Popovic [Realtime transcript read in error "Poparic"] allegedly had made?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, but we didn't have any of that information, I believe, at the time in 2000. I don't believe we reached the stage of the investigation where that could have been asked, if I put it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I'll just note for the record, since you bring it up, that when Mr. Nikolic testified, he wasn't asked a single question about that by the Defence which should have been done under 90(H).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That -- unless my colleagues have a question for you, that concludes your evidence, Mr. Uscumlic. On behalf of the Chamber, I'd like to thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll continue with Ms. Subotic's evidence. At line 13 on previous page, "Poparic" should read "Popovic."

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, while the witness comes in, could I ask the Registrar to bring up photograph number 65 ter 24355, which I believe was on the screen when we broke last week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning. [Interpretation] Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please continue, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, when we broke last week, we were in the process of looking at the photograph on the screen in front of you. Would you agree that this appears to show four rocket motors which appear to be attached in a manner which suggests that it was supposed to be attached to an air-bomb, and of course, there is a box of matches which has been put there, presumably, to show the scale of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you. This may have been attached to an air-bomb.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, you said in your earlier evidence at page 38497 that the coaxiality between the rocket force and the projectile itself is very important. Moving on from that assertion, it's correct, isn't it, that for this modified air-bomb to be accurate, it's vital that each rocket is connected in a manner that it is exactly parallel to each other rocket and also that it is exactly parallel to the air-bomb?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the longitudinal axis of the air-bomb.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I tender that photograph, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6326, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, would you agree that any of the modified air-bombs discussed in your report, including the rocket-assisted portions of those modified air-bombs, as well as the launch systems for the modified air-bombs, all of those would have to be manufactured under tightly controlled factory conditions and thoroughly tested before being approved for use?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Would you also agree that to fire any of those modified air-bombs with accuracy you would need detailed firing tables? Those firing tables would have to take into account factors such as the mass and propulsive force used for each kind of modified air-bomb, as well as other effects including crosswind, air temperature, air pressure, and other relevant factors?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A few days ago I said in this courtroom that such results couldn't have been obtained without firing tables, and any firing table includes what you have listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And did the Defence team provide to you any copies of contemporaneous firing tables for any of the modified air-bombs' systems that you discuss in your report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did the Defence provide you with any test data for the modified air-bombs themselves or for the launch systems for the modified air-bombs?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were some documents about launchers or air-bombs to be sent for testing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, I've read your report --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it wasn't important to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I've read your reports very carefully, and you haven't referred to any contemporaneous test data for the modified air-bombs that you discussed. You've worked at the Military Technical Institute in Belgrade for 35 years; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And that is the preeminent testing ground, or it was in the pre-war period, for the entire Yugoslav weapons industry. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were in research and development, and we also dealt with auxiliary development until a device was licensed for use in the armed forces. However, testing was done elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And indeed in your evidence in chief, you referred --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The technical operative centre, and it was -- and the persons involved were Poparic and Andjelkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Line 24, "However, testing was done elsewhere," but the witness stated very accurately where it was done, but it was not recorded. Oh, I can see there is something on the following page. I'd kindly like Mr. Gaynor to elicit a complete answer from the witness about the place where testing was done, both the name of the institution and the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, yes, I can approach it from a different route.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic, you said in your evidence in chief that you tested some of the assets to design firing tables. That was at page 38232, and you know that assets were tested in Nikinci. Did you participate in the testing of modified air-bombs, or have you seen any test data for the testing of modified air-bombs anywhere, whether in Serbia or Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, first of all, in the examination-in-chief I said I took part in the testing of many assets, which is true, but the main purpose of my institution, that is where I worked, was not really testing. We tested in order to verify our project or designs, but the technical testing centre was the main institution in charge of that. But I personally never tested a modified air-bomb. I saw documents, though, stating -- I mean documents from this trial, but these documents were not interesting to me for my report, and according to these documents, launchers were sent to be tested. Of course, I cannot quote from these documents, but the Defence team may be able to provide them. I think they were sent to the overhaul centre of Kragujevac, to the repair centre of Kragujevac, and it follows that a launcher and the bombs themselves were tested. I only saw documents to that effect, but I personally didn't test them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic, given the importance of test data in the context of your report where you are asserting that these modified air-bombs were accurate weapons, it is extremely surprising, is it not, that you did not refer to that test data in your report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, in this report it was not necessary to cite that data, because it was not required for this purpose. We did some tests on the ground, and these can be considered experiments. And from that aspect, an analysis was carried out about accuracy. And one product, specifically a modified air-bomb, met the technical conditions for rocket artillery. If you look at the firing tables of Orkan or Oganj and so on, they all match what we established on the ground. So it was -- the analysis was carried out from this point of view and not as you described it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is from the point of view of the impact at target.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask the Registrar, please, for D3540, page 66 in English and page 64 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What's coming up now is your air-bombs report. You turn to page 64 in your version, Ms. Subotic, to footnote 118. I'll just read it out. That footnote reads in part: "Aerodynamic coefficients were calculated and confirmed by experiment when firing tables were being made for the aircraft bomb, and thrust parameters of the rocket motor were taken from the test station during testing." That is the end of that quote. Now, it's correct, isn't it, Ms. Subotic, that what you did is that you took test results for an air-bomb when it is used as an air-bomb, and you combined those with test results for a rocket when it is used as a rocket, and you attempted to fuse those results together to try to figure out how a modified air-bomb, which is aerodynamically totally different to an air-bomb or a rocket, you attempted to fuse those results together to provide results which you are presenting as reliable results. Isn't that what you did?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You must understand, first of all, that an aerodynamic definition of any projectile, including the ball of yours, is obtained by testing in an aerodynamic tunnel. That is, we design it, make a model, and put it into an aerodynamic tunnel and test it in a -- under certain wind speeds. And the way a projectile flies is defined by the shape, which does not change, and by the -- by the wind speed, which also is not changed. A launching of a projectile from the ground is -- does not differ in that sense, so there are no aerodynamic differences. When I say experimentally, I mean that. When I speak about the motor, then the motor is tested the way it's always tested, that is, at the testing bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic -- Mrs. Subotic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last part of her answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I kindly ask for something to be done about the transcript. Could Mrs. Subotic please speak more slowly, and the transcript should also be reviewed and amended, because it is a disaster.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you speak more slowly. Yes. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Finally on this point, it's correct, isn't it, Mrs. Subotic, that nowhere in the many hundreds of footnotes your report and in the report that you coauthored with Mr. Poparic do you refer to the existence of contemporaneous, that is to say, from 1994, 1995, firing tables for the modified air-bomb system, nor do you rely on the test data for the modified air-bomb system when used as a modified air-bomb, nor do you rely on contemporaneous test data for any launch system for the modified air-bomb systems that you describe in your report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. However, I did tell you during that first week when we met at the Tribunal that the method which was used for these analyses was accurate within the margin of up to 3 per cent, and this has been verified. We always produced -- produce firing tables in advance, before any testing takes place, and the differences that emerge during these tests do not exceed several percentage units. This could not have been done better, because simply we did not have the firing tables that must have existed. They must have existed clearly based on the situation on the ground. This was worked out in detail. The mathematical model that was used was one that was used for decades with various modifications and changes, and its range of accuracy or margin of error again is 3 per cent. And I did say that we fitted all the aerodynamic characteristics that came out as a result of the tunnel testing and the gaseous effects of the engine as a result of the testing which is normally done when one produces the firing table. So the experiments that were done served to confirm our own calculations.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even though we found the documents that the air-bombs and the launch system were sent out for testing, we did not find among the material provided to us from the court any documents that would show the test -- test results, the results of these very tests. And of course you will understand that we cannot use something that we do not have.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic, in your evidence in chief at page 38206, you claimed: "According to the calculations and the tables for one projectile propelled by rockets FAB-100, 1VD, so one probable table deviation is 102 metres ..." You're claiming that a FAB-100 modified air-bomb has a deviation of 102 metres. Now, is that its deviation laterally or longitudinally? This was in your oral evidence, not in your report. It doesn't appear in your report.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is radial deviation. We worked with radial deviation in this instance precisely so as not to end up in a situation where we would not accurately determine the direction or the trajectory. So we would be proceeding on an erroneous basis. That's why we used the so-called radial deviation. And in the table, which deals with this dispersion, the FAB-100 has 43 metres in length, 98 in longitudinal direction, and the 100 that you quote is in fact radial deviation. So this would be the trigonometric mean. The Pythagorus theorem would actually -- this would actually relate --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please repeat slowly what she just said about the Pythagorus theorem.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you repeat from after the Pythagorus theorem, please, Mrs. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The radial deviation that we used in your analysis in order to increase the accuracy of what we are dealing with since we don't know exactly the trajectory, we applied radial deviations, and this is done in such a way that you would have a square root of the deviations and the square root of such a diagram would actually yield 50 per cent -- per cent probability of -- of those kits.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this is what we call probable radial deviation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic, I put it to you that you really didn't have any idea whatsoever how accurate the modified air-bomb system, any of the four that you described in your report, was, because you had no access to reliable test data, possibly because that test data didn't exist, and you did not have any access whatsoever to firing tables, possibly because proper firing tables didn't exist either, and you are not in a position to give this Court the assertion that some kind of radial deviation of 102 metres existed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor, I apprehend that you're putting your case to the witness, are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Now, is it possible that you could dismantle it just a bit --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: -- so that we can have it in bits that she could answer as we go along.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Right. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I will cut my question down, Mrs. Subotic. I'm putting it to you that you did not have access to contemporaneous test data or contemporaneous firing tables. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to make such an analysis, I do not need the tables. That's under one. If you allow me to say this, I have been producing the tables for the past 35 years, and I'm not in a position where I need to read other people's firing tables in order to analyse it, something that happened in reality and where I have information from the ground. That's under number one. Number two, you are making assertions that fall into my profession, and you will concede that I do know a bit more about it, a bit more, so I can assess the accuracy of my findings, and I can stand by them. If you or the Trial Chamber were in agreement, I would indeed be happy to make such an experiment. We -- this is something that could be done. We can organise testing, and then we can test both your assertion and mine. In this same expert report that you have in front of you, among those listed there is a product that my country offered for sale, which is very similar to the asset that we are talking about here. There are firing tables for that particular product of ours which do not differ at all from what I calculated. What is offered as a warhead element with it, is somewhat different from what was used during the war, but I can match these firing tables, and we can double-check them and put this discussion to an end at last. So you'll allow that if I say that something was done as per an experiment that has been done in the same way for the past 50 years, and when I say that the measurements were taken in an aero tunnel, and when I say that these forces were measured on the table, then you can conclude that they are completely valid and accurate as measurements. What we are discussing in terms of accuracy, and of course it was necessary to test the asset in summertime conditions, we are talking about the technical details of the launching process itself of possibly some other specific detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic, could I ask you to keep your, subject to the direction of the Trial Chamber, answers concise and to the point. I'm going to put to you a couple of questions. I'd be grateful if you could answer with a yes or no. Have you received any formal military training in target selection?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The question --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In target selection? Military training?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. I'll repeat my question. Have you received, from the JNA or any other army, any formal training in the art or science of target selection?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not had any such training. In the institution where I worked, the person responsible for all the sort of training and who has undergone all these trainings will be the one who will issue me with requests for testing or anything else that needs to be done which I will then do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did the Defence provide to you any target lists created by the VRS?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. When you talk of targets, my understanding of it is that it is some sort of an aim, an objective.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. -- Mrs. Subotic?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'll explain. In your report, for example at paragraph 158, you say that the Aleksa Santic primary school was the most likely target for the G10 incident. At paragraph 159, you say that the Zica factory was the most likely target for the G11 incident. In paragraph 161 you say that the BH TV building was the most likely target for the G13 incident. At paragraph 163 you say that the Bitumenka factory was the most likely target for the G15 incident. My question is: Did the Defence provide you with any VRS documents suggesting that those were the targets intended in each of those incidents?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I understand your question. No. The Defence did not provide me anything of the sort. But you have to understand that each one of these targets was defined on the basis of the external ballistic parameters and the parameters of my professions. Each and every of these targets was along the line of fire in the area which was ballistically defined, and it was on this basis that they were determined, on the basis of the flight trajectory which always went across such target or was near such a target. And it was based on the dispersion pattern of the projectile and based on the parameters of my profession of ballistics that this was defined. It had nothing to do with the military doctrine or anything like that. In a word, what was said in the paragraphs that you cited was defined on the basis of my training and on the basis of the parameters of the projectile, the launching system, the point of launch, and the point of impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask the Registrar to bring up page 188 of this document in English. It's page 181 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's the version you have in front of you, of course, Mrs. Subotic. This is a table. In the second column from the left, column number 2, you state: "Most probable target," and you've just given us a helpful indication of how you found out what that target was. Now, I am going to put an assertion to you, Mrs. Subotic, and that is that you have, in fact, engaged in a process of seeing where the projectile landed and trying to figure out what kind of military target was in the vicinity of the impact point. Isn't that right? Or along the trajectory of the projectile.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, in order to make an analysis of precision to begin with, in my line of work one has to know where this is located in relation to the target. In each and every one of these cases involving projectiles, I didn't look for particular features, but all of them were either on the incoming trajectory or close to the incoming trajectory of the projectile. I didn't go looking for them. They were there in the vicinity, and it -- it was in all of these 15 or 16 cases. It wasn't an isolated case, and it wasn't the case of me finding a building that was conveniently close. In order to make an analysis or precision, we cannot look at the image of Sarajevo and say, well, there were some 15 or 16 or how many projectiles that landed, and let's see what the dispersion pattern was, without knowing what the target was. This is impossible in my line of work, and it would mean nothing to me, to you, or to this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So every time in the immediate vicinity along the incoming trajectory of these projectiles there was a target which, as you noted, we, or I, if you will, designated as the most likely.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Subotic. We've going to move now to your report about the Markale I incident and the Markale II incident. You can pull that out if you wish, subject to the direction of the Trial Chamber. Your report is D3551. Now, in your report, in respect of the Markale I incident, you state that you believe that this was "a well-planned, organised and implemented act of sabotage." And I want to go through the stages of that well-planned, organised and implemented act of sabotage.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask the Registrar, please, to bring up page 80 in English and page 122 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, at the bottom of that page we see your statement which is in bold. You state that: "It is certain that on 5th of February, 1994, a mortar shell did not land at the Markale market, but, rather, a mortar shell," and if we can turn to the next page, please, "activated in static conditions exploded." Elsewhere in your report you say, in the next paragraph, in fact, that there was, in fact, another explosion at the moment when the 120-millimetre mortar shell exploded at the market.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. 120.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe that's what I said. Now, if we go to the section marked "Static Explosion," it is headed with (d), I'd like to take the Trial Chamber through three stages, which, if your theory is to be accepted, must have taken place. The first is the placement of the two mortars on a stand. If we see the first paragraph of the subsection headed "Static Explosion," you say that mortar shells without stabilisers were most likely placed on a stand support which ensured that the mortar shell would have an angle of around 60 degrees relative to the horizon angle of descent and an angle of around 57 degrees relative to a direction, azimuth, ensuring an azimuth angle of 18 degrees. Mrs. Subotic, could you clarify whether both of the mortars or just one was set up on a stand in this way? Just clarify, two or one?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A mortar -- or, rather, the mortar projectile which was analysed which had an azimuth of 18 degrees was placed at an angle of 60 degrees. We don't know about the other one, though. Colleague Zecevic marked the point of impact. We have splinter grooves in the area between Marsala Tita and Dzenetica Cikma Street as indicated in the report, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now could you confirm for my understanding that for your theory to be correct, the sabotage team would have had to carry out measurements in advance of placing that mortar on the stand, those measurements clearly calculated to make it look as if the mortar had come from Bosnian Serb territory? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid the interpretation doesn't go the same way as your words, because the mortar projectile is being confused with the mortars. I'm not sure if you said that. Let me repeat what you said. You asked me if I was of the view that a mortar projectile, according to my analysis, was placed at an angle of 60 degrees on some sort of a stand in order to leave such a pattern on the ground which would normally be there had the projectile flown in under those conditions. Is that what you wanted to ask me?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No. We'll get to that point later. At the moment, is it right that under your --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the interpretation of your question that I received, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'll repeat my question. Under your theory, this highly organised sabotage team must have carried out measurements prior to placing the mortar on the stand, those measurements carefully calculated to be consistent with the mortar having come from Bosnian Serb-held territory; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At any rate, there is mention again of a mortar, which I don't see how it can be there in your question. At any rate, I will answer the question. The person who was in charge of this incident must have done good preparation, and I did say in my report that these preparations were well organised. However, there were certain flaws in that preparation which allowed us to come to the conclusion that this was not the way things happened. Quite a few parameters were taken care of, and what was done was a good attempt to leave an impression, but none of us really addressed the issue of whether this could have happened in view of the place where the projectile really landed and what it had to steer clear of in its trajectory in order to land there. But, yes, the answer to your question is that what was done there was done very well and even very professionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to move now to the detonation question. It's your position, isn't it, that the two mortar bombs were detonated either using a timer or a remote control device; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the transcript what is missing throughout is a highly professional person rather than very professionally. [In English] Not very professionally, but person, highly professional.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't see much difference. Let's continue. I think the witness answered yes to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, do you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. It was certainly a professional who did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic, you agreed earlier in your oral evidence to a question -- in response to a question from Judge Morrison --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. It's not reflected. Could you repeat your previous question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you mean the question that I've just asked, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. The witness answered to the different -- when asked whether it's your position that the two mortar bombs were detonated either using a timer or a remote control device, your answer was yes; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: In response to a question from Judge Morrison - this appears at page 38389 - you agreed that unless the secondary device which must have been attached to each of the mortar bombs was vapourized in the explosion, you would expect to find physical evidence of that secondary device at the scene; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. In principle, it should have been found. However, you are the witness, we're all witnesses that not even the entire pieces of rocket engines were found. A point of explosion is not where you can find every single fragment. In the document that we just saw, we saw that in every other incident there was the number of engines that is in dispute, and those would have been huge pieces that should have been found on the spot. So the answer is yes. However, it is also logical that they wouldn't be found because they would be very tiny. And as we all know, a point of explosion is a place where pieces fly all over the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, you accept, just say yes or no to this, that there is no evidence in what you've inspected to suggest that physical remains of a timer or a remote control secondary device was found at the scene; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I was not the one who examined the points of explosion. It was the CSB who did that. I was not the one. It was the CSB. What they found was the only piece of information that I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And if they didn't find things, I can't tell you that those things never existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd now like to move to the second stage, which is on the next page in B/C/S, and this page in English. This is the post-detonation stage, and it says there that: "After the explosions of the mortar shells, organised activities started to create an impression of the horrible disaster. A BH TV crew is very quickly at this scene and at the Kosevo Hospital." You go on to say that: "Horrible scenes of casualties are recorded, but the point of the impact of the projectile is not shown until UNPROFOR representatives show up at the scene one hour after the explosion. On that occasion, already dead persons are brought to the market, and they are dragged through the market leaving a strong impression on everyone who watches these scenes. Certain persons are assigned to bring body parts in front of the cameras," and so on. Now, I'd like to ask you a few questions which flow from this stage of your theory. First of all, after the two bombs exploded in the market-place, that twin detonation must have killed a lot of people; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. That must have been the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: So it's your evidence that there must have been bodies in the market-place of those who were killed in that twin detonation, and then very quickly more bodies were brought into the market-place and scattered or placed around the bodies of those who had just been killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, those who had just been killed were removed within five -- 15 minutes, in a rapid action that ensued and that was described in detail in the findings. I don't want to repeat it. Those who were injured were taken away. I'm talking about a different thing here. I'm talking about certain things that in my view -- in my view were used to increase the horrendity of the scene, because when we watch the films carefully we saw that some scenes were repeated, that some people were moved, that there was no blood under them, that one and the same person checked in all places whether somebody was injured or not, and then in the later course of the film you could see that that person was not alive at all, and he was carried along the market. If you watch those films in detail, you will see all that, but that's what you will see, and that was what was blown up for the media. Having said that, I'm not claiming that there were no casualties. There must have been. All the individuals -- individual observations are provided. I don't see what else I could add to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you about the bodies which under your theory were brought into the market-place. It follows, does it not, that there must have been a pile of bodies dressed in civilian clothing stored very close to the market place prior to the incident.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there is a military lorry depicted in the film next to the market-place, and that was moments after the explosion which you can glean from other elements that were provided by the witnesses. People were still running out of the market-place. Second of all, it is stated that there were a series of illogical things there that indicated that those activities did happen. There is a lorry coming together with an ambulance. The door is open, and it comes from the direction of Marsala Tita Street, and in there you can already see a body. You can see that depicted in the film. We just pointed to some of the facts, that everything depicted very well in the video-clip. There is also a situation in which vehicles are moving in the direction opposite to the direction of the traffic at the beginning of the evacuation. The police themselves arrived at the very end of the evacuation, and in the meantime there were a lot of people with badges who were in charge of the evacuation, who organised the evacuation. That evacuation was carried out through an adjacent street, and the only thing that qualifies it is the vicinity of the place of the explosion. Dzenetica Cikma is very close to the place of incident at the exit of the market. There is a series of parameters indicating that the organisation was what it was and what is given in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, in your report you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- I see the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. We'll have a break for half an hour and resume at 10 past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic, in a moment we will see the video in question, and in that video there is a great deal of what appears to be blood. Is it your position that that is real blood or fake blood? Is the blood in the video real blood or fake blood?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought that you were going to show me the clip. That's why I paused. Of course, everything, all the blood that you see in the video-clip, in my view, is real blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: But several of the bodies were dragged and placed at the site after the detonation; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stated in our report all of those places that we had observed and that indicated that fact. We did not count those bodies. We just mentioned the fact. We pointed to the phenomenon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Please identify the number of minutes which elapsed between bringing the bodies from wherever they were stored prior to the incident to Markale Market and then bringing those same bodies to Kosevo Hospital.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand your question. In any case, the whole evacuation lasted not more than 20 minutes, between 15 and 20 minutes at the most judging by the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It follows, does it not, that the bodies must have been taken from wherever they were stored prior to the detonation, placed in the market-place by what you've described as a well-organised sabotage team, and then those same bodies were brought to Kosevo Hospital within those 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Perhaps now we can go to the video. And I believe under your theory, the BiH -- the television crew was part of the conspiracy; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what is depicted in the video-clip, the TV crew was already there on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like now for the video to be played. This is 65 ter number 40622A. This is the version of the video which is, in fact, cited by Mrs. Subotic in her report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sorry, could I ask the technical booth to turn the sound on to the maximum volume, please. If we could start the video again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The technical booth will take a look at it. We need to wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Perhaps I just can take advantage of the pause to ask you one or two questions about modified air-bombs, Mrs. Subotic. We're just going to wait for the technical problems to be sorted out. Very often in your oral evidence you referred to ricochets of modified air-bombs; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how often, but in any case, modified air-bombs and their ricochets were mentioned at Aleksa Santic number 53 and on the studio C roof the BiH Radio and Television building. In those two incidents that indeed happened. I don't know if I mentioned that with regard to Zecevic's findings. I suppose I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, is it correct that modified air-bombs tend to ricochet because the fuse on the nose of the air-bomb is designed and tested for a near vertical impact?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First and foremost, ricochet is a consequence of the shape of the warhead and its front part. A fuse is an auxiliary part, because if it is affected during any kind of fall, the bomb will be activated. We're talking about the oval front part of the warhead, and this is something that has an effect on ricochet. And the bombs that were launched here were very close to horizontal trajectory, which means that the elevation angle on launching was very small, and as a result we have ricochet as a direct consequence together with the outer shape of the warhead.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm told that it should be okay by now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Perhaps we can start the video from the beginning, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Stop, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, in -- first of all, can you confirm that this is the video --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We've stopped at 22:43.8.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: First of all, confirm that this is, in fact, a video that you relied upon in your report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Second, at page 63 in the B/C/S, you have photograph numbered 38 is the image which is on the television screen right now, and you state that this man "was probably brought to that place after the explosion." That's at page 43 in the English. Could you clarify for the Trial Chamber how exactly that body was brought and placed in that place after the explosion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we zoom in on image 38?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all -- first of all, the text describes figure 37, not figure 38. Figure 38 shows a man in white trousers and a padded jacket. Throughout the entire clip he walks around and checks whether people are alive or dead. I assume that that's what he does. And the text that refers to figures 38 and 39 is about the figures, and it reads: "The same man in white pants and in a padded jacket checks whether people are alive or dead," which points to the fact that this is not just done by chance. Figure 38 is a man on the asphalt without any traces of blood around him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Just answer very briefly. We've got your report. How under your theory did this body end up in that location --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't see any traces of blood in the spot where this person is lying. There's no traces of blood whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic, my question is not whether there are traces of blood. My question is how did that body end up in the middle of the market-place after the detonation?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that his body was brought there. There are parts of this video-clip that have not been shown where you can see that nylon foils are pulled out from beneath the bodies, and the bodies are then left lying in those places.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If I could --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is also part of this video-clip. There are images of that. At the very beginning of the film, maybe you noticed it, while people are running around because of the detonation, at the very entrance of Marsala Tita Street there was a military lorry parked right before the evacuation started. I'm sure that you must have seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We're going to play the video from exactly where we left off now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Stop, please. We stopped at the mark 23:01.4.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, on page 64 of your report, picture number 40, you identify this figure which appears to be a woman in a black and white chequered coat as another body which has been deliberately placed in the market-place, presumably by the very well-organised sabotage crew; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In any case, what is in the report is the fact that traces of blood do not match the type of injuries, which is illustrated by photo 41. Her foot is completely severed, her injuries are tremendous. However, there are not as many traces of blood in the place where she was injured. That's why we concluded that the injuries do not match the traces of blood in the video-clip, which also indicates that that woman was also not injured in that place. However, her injuries are quite considerable.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, it follows from your theory that the sabotage crew must have had access to a great number of human beings who were dead and who were in civilian clothing and who bore signs of injuries consistent with the detonation of a mortar projectile; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're not talking about numbers here. We're talking about certain things that are registered in the video-clip which do not tally with the general picture of the injuries which can occur and which can result in the appearance of a detonation spot after detonation. We did not count the bodies. We did not mention any figures. In the findings and in the report, we provide all the analysis of all the figures of the injured and the dead who were registered during the investigations, and there are most incredible differences between those figures, really incredible differences.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, I'd like us to play on from precisely the moment where we stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Stop there, please. We've stopped at 24:16.6.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, is it your evidence that this body was placed at the market-place after the detonation, or is it your evidence that this person was killed in the detonation?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This person was most probably killed in the detonation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, of the bodies that we've seen so far, could you give the Trial Chamber an indication of what proportion were placed at the incident site after the detonation and what proportion were genuinely killed in what you've described as a double detonation?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the very beginning of this report an analysis was made of all -- or perhaps a bit further back, it doesn't matter, of the number of those killed and injured in this incident. The table is on page 82. It's table 1. And this is a summary of -- based on all the documents, about the number of injured and killed persons. We read the lists of injured persons taken to hospitals. We were very meticulous about it, but it is impossible to give a share as you try to elicit with your question. It -- it has been seen that the number of those killed varies from 51 to 69 and that those injured from 119 to 264 and so on. If I -- if I'm speaking from the point of view of my profession, then these numbers are highly questionable taking into account what can be done with a 120-millimetre mortar shell. So we conducted an analysis and concluded that the real number is much below those stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our analysis was made from the aspect of the average number of persons present in that market and so on, and I cannot give you any estimate aspiring to be accurate because it is simply impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We're going to play on from the precise moment we stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Stop, please. We stopped at 26:47.4.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Several times, I think, in the video we've seen what is clearly a prosthetic lower leg, and in many of the shots it is clear that it is a hollow prosthetic lower leg. And in your report at paragraph 32, you argue that this prosthetic leg is very similar to the prosthetic leg of Camil Begic who was killed at Markale on this day but it is slightly different to his prosthetic leg, and you also assert that this particular prosthetic leg was planted at the market-place; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That prosthetic leg certainly changed positions during the video-clip, and that was documented in the report. This was done a number of times. Nobody's denying that the -- the owner of that prosthetic leg was killed at Markale on that day. However, this prosthetic leg differs from the one shown in the courtroom. This has been observed, and we made a note of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, my question to you is we've all seen some very graphic scenes of this market-place. Please help me understand why this highly sophisticated sabotage team would want to place a prosthetic human leg at the scene if they had ready access to a great number of dead human bodies in civilian clothing with injuries consistent with the detonation of a mortar round?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I've been asking myself, too, and I have no other answer but that it contributed to creating an even more gruesome picture. It was -- and it is true that it is different from the one that has been brought to the courtroom and that its -- it was shown a number of times in this video-clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we play on from exactly where we stopped, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Stop, please. Thank you very much. That's at 29:33.7.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: At page 65 in the B/C/S version of your report, you have a photograph which appears to be from approximately this part of the video this man appears to be holding the very lower legs of what appear to be either one or two human beings who have been killed in the explosion. Your evidence on this point is unclear. Could you clarify whether it is your evidence that these two legs were planted at the market-place after the detonation?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course not, and I don't know how you arrived at that conclusion. The comment is about these parts of the body being carried around the market-place and not that they were brought there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And -- and they were videotaped a number of times, because in figure 45, they're carried by someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. I'll read out the English version of what you said. You said: "Someone is putting these boots here in a bag carried by a military policeman in such a way that they fully stick out of the bag --"
