utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Paragraph number?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sorry, this is on page 44 of the English version, paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Para number.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Paragraph 28. And she goes on to say: "... and are visible in entirety. This military policeman then takes these boots to Marsala Tita Street where there are many reporters. Everything indicates that this scene was also planned in advance."

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very briefly, just clarify for us what you meant that this scene was planned in advance. Did this soldier happen to have access to the mutilated lower legs of one or two human beings in order to show to the world's press?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of this text is to point out that these parts of a human body that can be seen in figure 42 were taken from one place in the market to Marsala Tita Street to another place in the market so as to be shown to the media and no more than that. This is a great human tragedy which was used for giving the event more media significance.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: This --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And there are other details in this video-tape that also show how tragic this was. I mean, if these two body parts had to be removed, then I don't understand why they were put in a bag and taken to Marsala Tita Street instead of being removed with all other body parts that were taken away on those roof parts except if the intention was to give the incident more significance. This was -- or, rather, this is the meaning of this text.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to tender the video at this stage, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: From -- could you give us the time-frame? In its entirety?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: In its entirety until the point that we've stopped at, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6327, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd now like to turn to your report, Mrs. Subotic, page 123 in the B/C/S and page 82 in the English, and this is the third of the three stages of this enormously sophisticated act of sabotage that I would like to address. I'd like to -- this -- this stage concerns the stabiliser. Now, you've already explained in your report that of the two rounds which detonated, the stabilisers were removed from both rounds, and then the next stage is that a stabiliser was buried underground. So let's look at what you had to say. You say: "We do not rule out the possibility that it was put there even before the explosion, and this is indicated by the hard-packed material in the layer above it. The stabiliser was not painted and came out of the wartime production of the Bosnian Serbs. This points even more to the Serbs as perpetrators of the crime. After the removal of the stabiliser by UNPROFOR, the crater was probably prepared in such a way that the axis of the crater had an angle of 60 degrees relative to the vertical angle of descent. Probably due to haste the hole was not prepared for the arrival of the next UNPROFOR team so they did not even measure the angle, judging that that was not possible. After their departure, the hole was obviously prepared so that the next UNPROFOR team measured an angle of around 70 degrees. Since this angle was greater than the needed angle, the angle was corrected again so that all following investigating teams registered an angle of around 60 degrees." Now, in footnote 2 -- 288, you say that: "Static activation cannot ensure in any way that the stabiliser's in the crater so it was necessary to put it there subsequently." My first question is for you to clarify, was the stabiliser buried underground before the detonation or after the detonation?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, both options are equally possible. To my mind, it was probably buried before the explosion. But the second option, of which I say that it's equally possible, follows from the fact that investigative teams came there one after the other and drew different conclusions as to the depth of the crater. One said that it couldn't be established. There -- the removal was taped, and the difference between the depth of the crater as measured and the real length of the fin that do not match the video footage, which clearly shows that the fin is deeply buried in the crater. So if we disregard UNPROFOR's findings which day after day state different depths, it is probable that the angle was not as it should be and that's why it was corrected. And different investigating teams measured different crater depths. The first one was 9 centimetres, and then we end up with a video-tape showing that the fin is deeply buried. We know exactly how large such a fin is. We all saw it here at this Tribunal, and we can all also take a look at firing tables. So to sum up, due to different manipulation of this crater, this material was subsequently buried there. This -- we can consider their findings as partly accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: There is Subotic, could I ask you to keep your answers briefer and more concise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we please play P1711, please, from 26 minutes and 10 seconds to 27 minutes and 28 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you -- you will agree that that was footage taken from a building next to Markale Market showing what others believed to be the impact site for 120-millimetre mortar projectile fired from Bosnian Serb positions?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you clarify whether under your theory this crater is the crater for one of the two detonations or for both detonations?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This crater -- I apologise, but I cannot see the transcript, so I don't know if I'm speaking too fast. This crater is a consequence of a shell that was investigated. The other explosion wasn't investigated at all. We only established that there was a second explosion, and that was corroborated by a witness here in this courtroom, Mr. Berko Zecevic. And this crater is supposed to be the impact site of a shell that came from the Bosnian Serb position.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: For the record, I don't think Mr. Berko Zecevic has ever claimed that there were two detonations at Markale Market on this day, but for the moment, can I just ask you to clarify for us the shrapnel pattern which is not addressed in your theory. Is it your evidence that the shrapnel pattern was carefully created by the sabotage team so as to be consistent with the shrapnel pattern which would have appeared if the projectile had been fired from Bosnian Serb positions?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And that was described in detail, and it was achieved by removing the primer --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down and repeat these technical details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Since we are talking about technical details, I would ask you to speak more slowly. Could you repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. These traces simulate a full explosion that would have occurred if the shell had fallen under an angle of about 60 degrees. Actually, it doesn't really match it fully. We analysed this angle, although Mr. Gaynor claims the opposite, and we -- the result of our calculation was a different angle and not 60 degrees. Anyway, these traces on the ground simulate an explosion that occurred by a shell that flew in under an angle more or less like the one established by the CSB investigators. That's 60-odd degrees, and we have it -- we established it precisely on the basis of these traces. However, we were limited by the accuracy of the measurement conducted by the CSB investigators. We were in no position to measure ourselves. The angle they measured is somewhat larger than the one measured by Mr. Berko Zecevic in accordance with his method but which we have stated -- we have said several times that it is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to turn -- we can turn to the photograph you use in your report at page 92 in the B/C/S which shows a photograph of the stabiliser after some of the material which had covered it had been removed. Now, my question for you, Mrs. Subotic, is to explain to the Trial Chamber your theory regarding the burial of the stabiliser. First of all, those who buried the stabiliser obviously knew the exact depth to which they needed to bury it. Page 92 in your version. The sabotage crew --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not -- no interpretation for a long -- for the entire question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'll begin again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've not been receiving interpretation at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'll start again, Mrs. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Okay. Okay, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I wish to address your theory about the burial of the stabiliser prior to the event. First of all, is it correct that the person who buried the stabiliser must have had access to very precise ballistic data to figure out the exact depth to which the stabiliser should be buried so as to be consistent with it having been fired from Bosnian Serb positions?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, I don't see when the transcript is finished, so I hope I can start answering. No, he did not need any exceptionally ballistic data. The ballistic data is contained in firing table belonging to every mortar, and those firing tables were in possession of everybody, hopefully, at the time. It is well known that one would have to see a shell landing with a charge 3 or higher, and then the stabiliser can be buried in its totality. We were not in a position to test whether the stabiliser should have been completely embedded or not. It depends very much on the surface. The surface also played a role, not just the velocity. So it was sufficient for the person to have a 120-millimetre mortar firing table and to be aware of the facts that I've just mentioned, and that is that the charge should have been charge 3 or higher.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Second, is it your evidence that the person who buried the stabiliser had access to a jackhammer or some kind of heavy instrument to drill through the hard asphalt surface of Markale Market in order to bury the stabiliser to the correct depth?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, he must have used a tool. Perhaps not as heavy a building tool as that. A spade would have sufficed, because the UNPROFOR investigator didn't use much more than that to -- to dig it out. So any basic tools that can be found in basements and tool sheds could have been used. I'm sure that he did not have to have a jackhammer or any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic, have you ever tried to dig through a tarmac surface with a spade?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, of course not. However, I had my heel, a complete heel, get into the asphalt. Honestly, I don't want to interfere with other people's areas of expertise. I'm sure that he needed a tool of some sort, but whether that should have been a jackhammer, I'm really convinced that it didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, finally, I'd like to move to page 82 in the English, page 123 in the B/C/S, just to the four visits by the highly professional sabotage team to the impact point. The first visit was when they embedded the stabiliser. The second visit was after the stabiliser was removed in order to create a angle of descent of 60 degrees in the hole. The third visit was after Verdy was at the scene but before Russell got there, an hour after Verdy had left, to adjust the angle from 60 to 70 degrees. And the fourth visit was after Russell had left to adjust the angle back from 70 degrees to 60 degrees. Is my understanding of the sequence of events correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You understood the sequence really well, and now I'll try to explain things.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'm very pressed for time, Mrs. Subotic --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: She has to be able to explain and he shouldn't be pressed for time. We don't object. He can take as much as he wants. We think this evidence should be completely and fully tested, but she should have the right to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Fair enough. Please continue, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've just tried to explain things, but then I was interrupted. I don't know why. And this is what I wanted to say: Whether that happened in the way explained by Mr. Gaynor or whether the situation was prepared before the incident, whether the stabiliser was embedded and not tampered with subsequently is very difficult to say today, because there is a series of measures which do not tally, although they followed each other, and they don't even tally with the video-clip that we saw or the results that were obtained from the evidence. In other words, either corrections were made to the craters or the measurements were taken wrongly. In other words, we have to agree that we had to explain how those incongruent results could have happened, because they -- they could not have been caused by the incoming trajectory of the shell if the expert teams had taken the measurements correctly. This is how things could happen and no other way. If the measurements were correct. My view would be that the measurements were not taken correctly. The first measurement of the crater was 9 centimetres, and the stabiliser itself is longer than 9 centimetres, which means that between the moment the stabiliser was taken out and the subsequent measurement, the crater must have been filled in somehow.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic, could I please move to the question of the lethal radius of this event.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we move to page 85 in B/C/S. The relevant picture only exists in the B/C/S version, so we can look at it. If we could zoom in on the circle which is marked with a radius of 1056 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, that is, if I may suggest it to you, Mrs. Subotic, an astonishingly precise figure, and in your report I understand that you reached that figure from your observation of the video that we all saw earlier; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were watching the video, we actually established the perimeter around the market where we could see the traces of blood, and the figure was produced by AutoCAD and it was printed in the photo. Obviously there's no way to be so precise when taking measurements. It is just a factor of our analysis. This depicts a radius which is 105.6 [as interpreted] centimetres. It is certainly not the precise figure. When you do it in AutoCAD, the AutoCAD is responsible for the precise figure that it comes up with, but we as a team, we do not stand by it. We did not correct it because we don't see the reason why we should correct it after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I want to note for the transcript that the picture depicts a radius of 1056 centimetres. Clarify for us, is that the lethal radius for one detonation or for what you believe to have been two detonations?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the coverage area where you see traces of blood, and that was taken from the video-clip. I believe that the second detonation should have happened somewhere around here, but based on the sketch I can't tell you exactly where that red stall was. It should be somewhere here on the right-hand side of the sketch, in this passage, but I don't know exactly where. We did not analyse the distance. In general terms, we did not deal with two shells. We, rather, tried to establish the number of people who can fit in this area, and the rough estimate, and I repeat it was just a rough estimate, not the precise figure, and I'm sure that you realise that this was just one of the estimates that we analysed in order to come up with a ballpark figure of those who were dead and injured and that would have matched the assumed situation in which the explosion happened, and on the other hand, we tried to establish the lethal power of the asset itself. You probably know based on the analysis provided by the experts in the courtroom that the lethal power of an asset is tested in an area. One hit in one square metre [Realtime transcript read in error "centimetre"] is the ballpark at which we stop considering that -- that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. We lost the last part of that answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The end of my answer referred to the criterion according to which the distance is established at which an asset has lethal power, and it is believed that it is a distance where there is one piece of shrapnel in one square metre of obstacle when tested in testing conditions. I suppose that you will know what a test area is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now it is okay. However, in line 22, it says "centimetres," whereas the OBOR should be explained, because the interpreter doesn't seem to know what -- what that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I will leave it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic, you're aware that in the firing table for the 120-millimetre mortar projectile it is suggested that the lethal radius is 17 metres.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sure, of course, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'll move on. Now, the -- you were present in this courtroom or one of the courtrooms in this building when Ekrem Suljevic and Mirza Sabljica testified, is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You know from their written evidence that both were present on the crime scene on the day of this incident?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, yeah. I don't remember that it would be the case with Ekrem Suljevic, but if you say so, then I'll believe you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And you knew that both were employed by the RBiH MUP.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: So surely both of those men must have been involved in the conspiracy which you have suggested existed?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid that you misunderstood my evidence. I did not name the investigators in my findings and in my report as participants in any conspiracy. To the contrary, we had several occasions to convince ourselves that the investigators could hardly recognise the point of impact, that they were looking for the stabiliser on the roof. You can see that as noise in the background at the beginning of the video-clip that we saw or some other video-clip. And it was only after they were -- it was suggested where they should look and dig they started looking at the point of impact, because that point of impact was completely atypical and not very discernible. So I didn't name any of the investigators as members in the conspiracy. It would never have occurred to me to say that or think that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Nevertheless, the details of this vast conspiracy were not put to those two witnesses, were they?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. She's not in a position to be putting questions to witnesses even if she's present in a courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well. I'll move on from this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If I can just summarise your position on this issue and put something to you, Mrs. Subotic, you are asking this Court to believe that an extremely elaborate plot was planned and put in place involving two static explosions but one crater visible, a stabiliser deliberately buried underground, the transport of the bodies of many dead persons in civilian clothing to the market-place followed by their rapid transfer from the market-place to the Kosevo Hospital in an effort to make this look as if a mortar projectile had been fired by the VRS from Serb-held territory into the crowded market-place, killing many people there. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, we have to call a spade a spade. I have made a very serious analysis, and I presented in very uncertain technical terms that it was not possible for that projectile to come from and explode in the place where it exploded without having hit the roof above the stall. I used all the measurements that the investigators took during their investigation of the incident. Every single claim was tested, double tested, and treble tested, taking into account all the available evidence. The angles were determined with precision, because there was quite a range in the documents as well as the azimuth and the angle of descent. That may have satisfied the criteria of the impact position where the investigators investigated, and it was explicitly proven based on physical evidence that it was simply not possible. On the other hand, it was established that whatever may be seen in the video-clip points to the fact that it was a media event more than anything else, that there was a lot of media coverage. I'm not asking for anything from anybody. I just want you to understand that this is a very critical analysis which is based on physical evidence. What nobody has mentioned during the cross-examination is the fact that there is a lot more inconsistencies here. One of them is the shape of the stall. It was designed by Mr. Zecevic, and I believe that Mr. Sabljica told us that the sketch had originally been drafted by him. So the stall as it was sketched is not the real shape of the stall, and with its dimension it helped for the projectile to be found in the place where it could not have been found in real conditions when the stall was reconstructed based on the video-clip and based on what it really looked like. So what I expect from everybody is to take my detailed report seriously, because it is based on very serious analysis of physical evidence, to study my report and to make their own very serious conclusions based on that very thorough report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, just before we break for lunch, I'll just put it you to that I suggest that an infinitely more likely scenario and explanation of what happened on the 5th of February, 1994, was that a mortar projectile was, in fact, fired by the VRS from Serb-held territory into the crowded market-place, killing many people there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Yes. Do you agree with that or do you not? Do you agree with that suggestion, or do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't agree with that suggestion because all the physical evidence points to the contrary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'm happy to break now for lunch before we move to Markale II.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I don't want to delay our lunch but I'm wondering if the Prosecution is putting its case to Dr. Subotic, shouldn't they also be required to put to her how they believe that this projectile was able to land in the place where it did without hitting the stall, which is the basis of her conclusions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's -- it's for the Prosecution how he puts the case to the witness. We'll have a break for 45 minutes. --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Line 21, page 59, it was interpreted as "a lot of media coverage," but her idea was that it was well planned by the media. So the interpretation should have been different to reflect that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll resume at 17 past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Before I do so, I'd just like to request some further time from the Court. I note that this witness was originally scheduled to give her evidence in chief in two hours. She in fact took eight hours. I've had a word with Mr. Robinson, and he has indicated that the Defence has no objection to some extension of the cross-examination time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Fair enough, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We're going to turn now to the Markale II incident, and on the final page of your report, which is page 126 in English, you essentially summarise two possibilities. One is that it was statically activated and the other is that there was a roof-top delivery. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Furthermore, you also claim that bodies of a number of dead persons dressed in civilian clothing were planted at the scene of the crime. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Where? Where do I claim that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, we'll get to the specifics of that. If you're denying it at this point, that's fine. We'll go through the video to the precise references. Before we do so, I'd like to address the Cymbeline radar system.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If we could go to page 158 in B/C/S and page 103 in English. Now, if we could focus in on the diagram alone. It's not necessary, in fact, to see the English for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like you to clarify the source for some of this information. First of all, what does 548 metres represent?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 548 metres, that's the ordinate of the trajectory. We can see in the documents that a projectile flying at the altitude of 548 metres cannot be see on radar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well. Now, you have placed a representation of the centre point and the diameter, maximum diameter, of the radar's beam. The centre point appears to be of the order of 1.300 metres above Markale Market. What is your source for that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the documents available to me, the radar was positioned at a distance of about 1.000 metres, and it could catch all mortar shells with a trajectory above the ordinate I mentioned, and this follows from the radar position and the parameters found in the documents regarding the radar. According to my estimate, the radar was about a thousand-odd metres away, although the information can be found that the separation line was right there, but according to my information, it was at a distance of 2.000 metres. The position of the radar was excellently chosen, very professionally chosen, because it is at a place where all the trajectories meet, and only in this way was it possible to catch or cover every trajectory.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I want to return to the centre point of the radar beam. I don't believe you answered the question as to the source of your information for the radar beam having its centre point at an altitude of 1.300 metres above Markale Market. What is your source for that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. I never stated that information. I only stated the information found in the documents, namely, that it was placed at a distance of about 1.000 metres so as to be able to record every trajectory which is further away from 900 or 1.000 metres, and that is a quote. This -- the centre of the radar is not at an altitude, but it is so positioned that it can cover all trajectories, and that's what the documents clearly say. They also say that it was switched on 24 hours a day and that it could observe any trajectory of shells fired from VRS positions. I found that in UNPROFOR documents, and I give references for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic, in the UNPROFOR documents that you cite in your report, which are P1445 and specifically the memorandum from Colonel Brian E. Powers of G2 UNPROFOR to the UNPROFOR commander of 29 August 1995, do not contain any indication of the altitude of the centre point of the radar beam above Markale Market on the 28th of August, 1995. You have no source for the information in this graph regarding the centre point of the radar beam, do you?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we discussing this sketch, and have you read all these sketches and found that it says 1.300, because I never stated that. The position of the beam is immaterial. This sketch shows why the radar was unable to catch trajectories of shells coming from VRS positions, and I -- I really don't know where you found the value of 1.300 for the centre-piece of the radar. This sketch is meant to be an illustration. It does, however, include accurate data. The ordinate of the peak of the trajectory that goes right below the radar beam, and I don't know how -- how you came up with the value you stated for the radar centre-piece. And anyway, it is immaterial for the radar's ability to register trajectories.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic, for clarification, 1.300 metres is a figure that I determined based on analysis of your sketch. Now, I put it to you that you have no way of knowing three things: Number one, the centre point of the radar beam; number two, the radius of the radar beam which is in operation at the time; and number three, the location of the centre point of the radar beam in relation to Markale Market.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now you enumerated some things, and I'll answer in the same way. You -- there is an X axis here without dimensions, and on the basis of that you inferred an ordinate value. Secondly, you mistook a schematic representation for an accurate depiction, because in the latter case I would have given the ordinate values, and then you could have read them and interpreted the value that you say -- you stated. And I forget what it is that you mentioned third. This diagram does not have a scale, and it is merely an illustration to help the reader understand what is being discussed, and it is meant for you to read values from an ordinate which doesn't have a scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'm going to move on to another issue, and that is the location in which the Markale II stabiliser was found on the road. You have made it clear in your report, I think, that you consider a lateral movement of the stabiliser to be inconsistent with an impact arising due to the incoming stabiliser arriving from Bosnian Serb territory, roughly speaking, to the south of the market-place. Now, in your -- in your evidence in chief, you accepted the basic theory that where the kickback or the ejection force exceeds the inward force, that a stabiliser will be kicked back instead of being embedded in the ground. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that you're speaking about velocity rather than power. So the velocity at which the projectile flew in and the stabiliser was ejected from the body of the shell. In the case you described, it is most probable that the stabiliser is ejected during the -- during the flight to the place from which the shell originated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. It looks like we're in agreement. So during that rearward trajectory approximately heading back to where the projectile originated from, is it not right that in this case it would very likely have hit the building over which it had travelled prior to impact?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a remark about the transcript. At the end of the answer, there is or -- there is something missing. The witness said "in the direction where it came from or nearby." This "nearby" is missing. Lines 1 and 2 on page 66.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Subotic, I'm asking you to consider that instead of the stabiliser going back along its trajectory right back to where it had been fired from, what actually happened was it was kicked back and hit a building, which resulted in it being pushed in the lateral direction along the road.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do I put this. We know from physics that there's a law of action and reaction as a very common occurrence. If the stabiliser had hit a wall, as you said, when it was ejected, it would most probably have been launched in the direction from which it had come. That's the most probable outcome. Even if I accept your thesis, which is a little likely and would depend on many factors for which I have no parameters, we're speaking about 29 metres from -- sideways from the site of impact by a wall. According to your theory, what should have happened is what Mr. Zecevic called an impossible ricochet. The stabiliser was found right next to a wall according to the sketch that I saw, and that is at an angle -- at a right angle from its trajectory.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'll move to another issue now, and that is the batch numbers which appear on what you claim are three stabilisers and what the Prosecution believes is one stabiliser.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If we could turn now to page 153 in B/C/S, page 100 in English. If we could focus in on the three photographs on the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I believe it's your evidence, Mrs. Subotic, that we are looking at here are three very similar but, in fact, different stabilisers; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that in this photograph we see three stabilisers of which one is in the photo documentation, another was from the video-tape, probably the same, and the exhibit in this courtroom is different. Based on the positions marked here, and these are the positions for the tools used to charge it initially. This was taken by the French team, and you see clear signs of erosion, and it cannot be seen anywhere afterwards except in the video footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like the Registrar to show you, please, Exhibit P1454, and perhaps we could get a photograph of that exhibit onto the screen. This is an object which has been tendered to the Court as the stabiliser from the Markale II incident. Let's deal first with the question of the location of the two holes which are visible to all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Perhaps the Registrar could hand that object to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I think there's common ground that there is a photograph of this stabiliser which shows the holes in a slightly different position to how they appear in this photograph. Mrs. Subotic, I'm inviting you to consider the possibility that those who investigated this incident might have removed this cap as part of this investigation and then screwed it on again, resulting in a slightly different alignment of the holes. Do you accept that that is a possibility?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, that is totally unreal, because this is closed using a tool, and it is next to impossible to remove. The manufacturing process of this piece that I have in front of me is such that this is fixed with special tools, and it is also impossible to open. Now it's a bit shaky, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What do you mean by, "Now, it's a bit shaky"?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normally this is fixed. I can tell now that it has been unscrewed and screwed back on but I can't tell why.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: When.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was constructed in such a way as to be locked once it's screwed on. I don't see why anybody would want to open it except -- well, I really don't want to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I think we can agree for the purpose of the transcript, Mrs. Subotic, that you have with your fingers been able to move the positions of the holes at the top of this stabiliser right now in the courtroom. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can agree on that for the transcript, but I must add that I absolutely cannot determine why, when, and how it was done. It's a fact that this is closed with tools, very strong tools, because they need great force to do so. When and why this was done, I really don't want to speculate about, and I would like to state this for the transcript as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to move to the markings on the stabiliser. Is it correct that the stabiliser, which is physically next to you at this moment, as well as that photographed on the screen in front of you, bear the -- bear the characters MKM74 KB9307?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm holding in my hands is KB9307.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Correct. And I'm -- and on the other side of the stabiliser it says MKM74; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask the Registrar, please, to bring up P1971, photograph 23. If we could please zoom in as close as possible to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And I believe we can see the same characters appear on this photograph of what you consider to be a different projectile; is that -- a different stabiliser, correction.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, since you demonstrated to me that this was moving when I touched it, there is no reason for me to assume that it came here in any specific manner. So this could have been placed here from another stabiliser if it is not closed -- if it was -- if it isn't closed in the factory. So if it's not in the original state.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you accept that the expression KB are the Cyrillic -- are Cyrillic letters KV in Latin for Krusik Valjevo, and 9307 would suggest that this was manufactured at Krusik in Valjevo in July of 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is Krusik Valjevo. I heard something else in my headphones. Yes, of course. It's a marking -- it's a mark indicating the factory where it was manufactured.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I call up, please, 65 ter 2 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you kindly, since we're looking at this and this, if we put one next to the other, then we see that the marking on the primer is different from what I'm holding in my hand. I would like you to take a look at it too, because that indicates manipulation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The object I'm holding in my hand has a different mark on the primer than what we see in this photograph. This here is right of the centre, whereas this is centre left. The mark is downward under an angle of 45 degrees in the lower left quadrant of the coordinate system.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This should also be mentioned if we discuss differences and matches. This is a very good forensic example.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please do not overlap with the English translation. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it will be good if you asked the parallel -- that we see in parallel, P1454 and P1971.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Back to you, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. These are all matters which Mr. Karadzic can take up in re-examination. It's quite clear from the witness's report that she considers -- she's put forth a theory to Your Honours that there are three stabilisers extremely similarly shaped but with slight differences to them, and I will leave that assessment to Your Honours in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But your case is that what she holds at the moment is the identical one --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, that's right --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- with what we are seeing now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The Prosecution's case is that there is one Markale II stabiliser. It's photographed at the time, which is what we're looking at right now. It's sitting right now on the desk in front of Mrs. Subotic, and it's the same stabiliser that appears in all three photographs in her report. So I want to move to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But what she said right now -- I'm waiting. What she's said right now is that's different from what appears from the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. And in her report she goes through the reasons why she thinks there are three different stabilisers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But are you not minded to see how it looks like, whether there's a way or not? So why don't -- why don't you ask her to expand a bit more --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- how its different.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic, could you expand on why you think the object on the monitor in front of you is different to -- is different to the object in your hand?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Or can we put it on the ELMO so that we can see it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Also, Mr. President, I noticed I didn't understand the word "primer" that was being interpreted, so if somebody could think about trying to explain that to us.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I think it would be better to put two parallel photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please could you explain how they are different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We saw a while ago that the thing moved under my fingers. I don't want to speculate as to how that happens. However, if you look, the left stabiliser which is in the courtroom and the right-hand side one which is depicted in the photo, they're now placed in similar positions. Both are in similar positions. The markings are more or less in the same place, and now we are looking at the central point where the primer hit and activated, which is depicted by the central circle or the orange circle. That may be seen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you slow down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a forensic piece of evidence that when the primer was initiated, we can use it to identify the type of weapon. You can see that on the right-hand side that we see in e-court, that mark is moved from the centre to the right. That impression is moved rightward. In the original part, that impression is moved from the centre to the left -- left from the primer from the moment that there was an impact in the primer, and if you see harder, you cannot see it until the example that we have in the courtroom, there is a mark, a very fine mark in the lower left quadrant from the full circle which is about 90 -- or, rather, 180, around 200-odd degrees from the centre. Now you can see that mark. I'm pointing to it. I don't know whether you can see it. It is shiny, and it's very easy for me to see under light. However, what is important here that you can see that here on the right-hand side there is a shift to the right, and on the left there is a shift to the left. The impression of the primer. So this is the evidence of the weapon being fired in -- irrespective of what we are talking about, whether it was tampered with with somebody's finger like I could. I could move it with my own fingers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. You were strong enough to move around the cap. Could you do this again, do that again while our usher holds it on the ELMO? If you could move around the ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems that I've locked it now -- no. No, I can move it, yes. To be honest, I really don't want to volunteer any more comments, absolutely not, no. I did not see this when I held this piece of evidence in my hands for the first time. Maybe it was there. I just failed to notice it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, I'll leave it to you, but while you continue, the Chamber wants to take a look at the stabiliser.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Yes, the usher can provide it to the Chamber now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, would it be possible for her to mark on the screen the mark that she's described on the photo so that at least we can have that recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think at certain point of time our video captured both images. I'm confident. I will confirm with my Registrar, because we were able to see the ELMO, and this is in our e-court. At some point in time we can compare if necessary. Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Could I call up, please, 65 ter 25089.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: A word of warning, Mrs. Subotic, this is rather hard to read in the original, but it appears to be a test data from Nikinci, Serbia, in March 1994, and you can just see it in the fax header. That it is from Nikinci, Serbia, 1994. And if we look at the top right-hand version of this, we can see a reference to -- if you look under "ammunition," and you look on the fourth entry it says "Cap MKM74 series KV9307." Now, first of all, can you confirm that this document suggests that a batch of MKM74 KV9307 shells was tested at Nikinci in Serbia on the 28th of March, 1994, and that that is in fact a 120-millimetre mortar shell?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult to read indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please bear with me for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Perhaps the Registrar could zoom in on the area under the word "municija" in the top right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Super, actually, indeed. This is a detonation cap, MKM74 of a particular series, primer is MKM74. There is gunpowder and so on and so forth. This is the testing of M6253 mine testing with MK detonation cap, M74, and the basic charge M74, a certain gun power, additional charge, M74 under conditions of normal temperature in terms of ballistics conditions. Where it says MKM74 refers to the detonation cap. That's what I read here. Or primer. And, of course, it was tested in Nikinci.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And do you accept that --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, this was TV9401 series.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to have to ask you about that. Just look closely at the MKM74 line, and I suggest to you that it actually reads KV9307.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can we blow that one up a little more?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is MK --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is reading too fast.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the cap series, MKM74. And what we see in front of that is the mark for the detonation cap and the model.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to tender that document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6328, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'm going to work -- move now to a separate issue which is the territory to the south of Sarajevo which you inspected.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: This is at page 161 in B/C/S, page 105 in English. This is on her modified -- sorry, this is the Markale report, which is D3551.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, if we could focus in on that image, please, and specifically on what I'm going to describe as a pie slice. It is a slice of 5.000 metres in length, extending from 175 degrees to 150 degrees. I'd like you to give the Trial Chamber your best estimate as to what proportion of that pie slice you visually inspected in order to determine whether it would have been suitable for the firing of a 120-millimetre mortar projectile.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We visited the area together with our escorts in order to establish what the conditions were for placing a mortar. I believe that I mentioned the place where it was possible to place a mortar. It was just one place, and its azimuth marking is 176 degrees. I probably mentioned the name of the location and the distance at which it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and that was --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic, please look at the pie slice and tell the Trial Chamber whether you inspected half of that territory, a quarter of that territory, 100th of that territory. Please give your best estimate to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know what, we inspected practically the entire territory, but we didn't go step-by-step. I suppose this is understandable. We only had two days to inspect the area. We had to investigate all the incidents in -- including sniping, air-bomb, and Markale incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic, you accept that the footprint for a 120-millimetre mortar unit is about 2 square metres?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you saying that the traces originating from placing a 120-millimetre mortar? You were not referring to shells but to the asset. What I heard in the interpretation was a footprint -- the footprint of a 120-millimetre mortar shell but I suppose you meant mortar asset; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to understand that this is a heavy weaponry. Heavy weaponry, for it to be positioned in a location, it has to be pulled by a vehicle, and if we have the footprint of 2 square metres, that mortar has to be hauled to that area. If the area through which it has to be dragged is wooded, uneven, inaccessible, then it is not to be expected for those 2 square metres to be lowered from a helicopter into the future position of our mortar; right? This is the biggest mortar that an infantry unit has. It is not a held -- hand-held mortar like a 60- or 82-millimetre weapons which you can carry on your shoulder and you can place it wherever you want before you fire from it. It's a different type of asset.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic, the pie slice that we're looking at which has a side of 5.000 metres and an arc of 125 degrees has an area of 4.5 million square metres. Do you agree with that assertion?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I would need to do my maths. 4.5 million square metres is a -- kilometres is a lot. Sounds like a lot of territory, but you may be right. I would need to check. I would need to use my calculator in order to check that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: 4.5 million square metres. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I need to check. Let's say you're right pending my own calculation. I need to calculate.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness repeat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You will allow me to control your maths. I noted your figure down. I cannot either agree or disagree before making my own calculation. I suppose you don't need to wait for me to get hold of a calculator and then to check your figures, so we can perhaps move on and I will check your figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic, I'm putting it to you that you could not possibly have inspected every location within the pie slice which appears on your own report to determine whether a 120-millimetre mortar projectile could have been fired from that location in August 1995, especially given that you carried out your inspection in, I believe, 2010 or 2011. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I inspected the area in 2011. I agree that the plant life has changed from the moment of the incident. Obviously, as I have just told you, we did not comb every step of the area. There was no time for that. However, the technical parameters and the physical evidence that we found proved that to be unnecessary because the shell could not have arrived from any of these directions, and this was based on the technical parameters on the spot such as traces on the asphalt, that it was not caught by radar. I'm talking about the shell. There was no sound of a shell being launched. It was not as the experts of the international community claimed, and that was that the prior five shells and that one shell were all fired simultaneously or in a short sequence. In any case, there is a lot of physical evidence on the spot that indicate -- why would we have inspected -- or, rather, determined this to be 5.000 metres if the stabiliser did not end up imbedded in the surface as we know? We can talk about charge 1 and charge 2 only, and not the distances and your 4.5 million square metres as the area from which the shell was fired. If it had been fired from anywhere in that area, the stabiliser would have ended up embedded in the surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to move now to page 97 in the English and page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While we -- you do so, I instructed the Registrar to capture the image that appeared on our monitor when the stabiliser was put on the ELMO, but while the Chamber was moving the cap part on, i.e., while screwing it and unscrewing it, the position of the markings in the inner circle seems to have been moved again. So in order to be clear, I will ask the Registrar to put this stabiliser on the ELMO and to capture the image again to compare with the previous image.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Put it on the ELMO, and we'll show it on our monitor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My proposal would be for the Trial Chamber to look at P1415 and P1471 in parallel on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You can do that in your re-examination. Yes, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to understand me, you have to first look at the image that Mr. Gaynor showed in e-court. I would then have to put this in the same position, and then we could compare the two. Otherwise, we won't end up with much --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have later on the three images to compare. Let's put it on the ELMO and capture the image. I'm asking the Registrar -- the usher to put it on the ELMO. Then we'll ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you put it the other way around. Yes. No, I'm not asking you, Mrs. Subotic. I just wanted to capture the image as it is now, because I moved it around. Please hand it back to Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in that case it will be of no use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could we zoom in a bit further. Too bright. Yes. Capture this image. Yes. Yes. Do you have anything to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I don't know how much you will be able to see from this position and whether you will understand the two things that I tried to compare, because now the markings denoting the series are not in the same position. It would be much clearer if we could place this thing so as to be easier for comparison with the photo. Now it looks completely different than it looked when it was placed in the previous position. I can put it in that same position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: I think Judge Kwon's observation, and it's certainly mine, is that when you unscrew the outer ring, the position of the inner ring also changes as a function of that unscrewing. So it's not the two circles, being made of obviously different material, are not restricted in their movement. The second point I'd like you to deal with it while I think about it is this: That you can at the moment unscrew it easily by hand. The two major indentations one can see either side of the central indentation appears -- appear to be the holes for the tool that is used to screw or unscrew it, which is much like the mechanism you see on the back of some, for instance, diving watches so that they can be made watertight or airtight, and you would require that tool to screw it up tightly or, indeed, to unscrew it once it had been screwed up tightly. But other than that, to my eye, there is no locking mechanism, and you've suggested in your evidence that it was locked in place rather than screwed in place, and perhaps you'd like to deal with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I would request the Registry to offer the printout of two captured images to the parties after the hearing today. Yes. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We're done with that stabiliser.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Should we assign an exhibit number to the captured image at this stage?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Shall we give the two exhibit numbers to the captured images.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibits P6329 and Exhibit P6330, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic, I'd like now to move to your theory of a roof-top delivery, and I'd like to use as an aid page 147 in B/C/S, page 97 in English. You accept, I believe, that a mortar fuse - this is of your Markale report, which is D3551 - accept that a mortar fuse is armed only from the extreme acceleration which accompanies the firing of the mortar projectile.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the basic construction of this fuse. I already testified to that. However, that part or the function of the fuse can be completely switched off. It's not a problem at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well. And you see in front of you the diagram taken by the RBiH MUP of the Markale II incident which appears to suggest that the building was 11.45 metres in height and the impact point was, I think, 4.8 metres from the base of the building.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You're aware that a 120-millimetre mortar projectile weighs in or around 11 kilogrammes?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And do you accept that if you were to drop an object from the top of a building of approximately 11.45 metres, it would take about 1.6 metres -- correction, 1.6 seconds to fall to the ground?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can do the necessary maths. I cannot answer off-the-cuff. You know, I'm a professional. I like to do my calculation first before I answer. I do not expect that you have done your maths. I suppose that this is just your estimate. In any case, the calculation of the free fall is pretty simple. I can do it during the break. I simply don't like to use or speak of any technical parameters without having checked them first.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if you could come back to us if you have a different figure to work with, but I'm asking you to consider that the duration of fall was about --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said 1.6; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Approximately 1.6, I think. Now, in order for your theory of a roof-top delivery to be correct, the sabotage crew would first have had to change the fuse on the mortar radically to ensure that it would be armed for a roof-top delivery system, for a roof-top delivery. Then one or two men would have to throw an 11-kilogramme object such that it landed 4.8 metres away from the base of the building, and they would have to take cover instantly to avoid being killed by the resulting detonation. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is one of the descriptions of this incident, which is possible. I say one of the descriptions. I was very much on my guard lest I speculate. I provided all the options here and indicated everything that is technically not accountable. The only option that is technically possible is that, in that case, it was fired from a very short distance from the positions of the BH Army. I suppose that if nobody heard that, then the only thing we are left with is something akin to what you said. Not to say that it could have been thrown off a lower positioned window. It did not necessarily have to be the roof-top. We did not go into speculations, "What if"? We wanted to find an option that would fit with the physical evidence at the site. There is a great deal of physical evidence on the ground that cannot be explained with the -- with a shell flying in from the VRS positions, because nothing similar happened. Had the shell flown in from the VRS positions, it would have to be at least 2 kilometres away in order to use charge 3. You know, this was the basis of our calculations. That co-ordinate would have been registered by radar, probably some of the systems would have registered the launch. We would not have as much shattered glass outside as we can see in the footage had the explosion happened that way, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I further put it to you that for your theory of a roof-top delivery to be correct, the shrapnel pattern on the ground would have had to be arranged very carefully so as to be consistent with the firing of a mortar projectile from Bosnian Serb-held territory.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to respond to that. The pattern of dispersion on the ground indicates precisely the fact that it was not fired from the VRS territory because it is a shallow groove, barely visible, and indicative of the fact that the projectile had flown in from a relatively short distance away and that it was fired possibly with charge 1. That's what the pattern on the ground shows, nothing else. You have shallow grooves. If we look at the footage, we will see that they were so shallow as to have been covered in by dust.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, Mrs. Subotic, the explanation you've offered just now is entirely inconsistent with the only two explanations which you offer in your report, one of which is roof-top delivery and the other of which is static explosion by a projectile presumably placed in the middle of a busy road.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why you see it that way. It fully fits with it all. It is completely consistent with it. A static explosion would indeed have been possible as such. On the other hand, we have, as I said, the possibility that it had fallen at a low speed. We cannot look at each one of these traces in isolation. We have to look at them as a whole, and if we look at them as a whole, there is no other conclusion that we can draw but this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Subotic, in your report you've made a number of assertions about a video. Again, you've asserted that at least three of the figures in the video bear injuries inconsistent with a 120-millimetre mortar projectile. You appear to suggest that those bodies were moved to the incident site after detonation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to play the video for the Trial Chamber. It's P1450, and we'll play from 00:20 to 4:05. We'll stop once or twice during the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we switch to Sanction.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd request the technical booth to play this with the sound on to the maximum. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We seem to have a problem switching into e-court. Shall we have a break for five minutes? --- Break taken at 2.28 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor, I'm told that due to a technical difficulty, we cannot see the video at the moment. So unless you have any other things --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I can just put one question to her on one point and use up some time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Judge Morrison asked you a question, Mrs. Subotic about the base of the stabiliser which you held in your hand. He said, "But to my eye, there is no locking mechanism, and you suggested in your evidence that it was locked in place rather than screwed in place, and perhaps you'd like to deal with that." I don't believe you did, in fact, deal with that. Would you like to do so now?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have an opportunity to answer, because other questions were then put to me. So I will answer now. There is no locking-in mechanism. When I said that it was locked, I meant that it was tightened with a tool and that the force was strong enough with which it was done that nothing would be shifted or changed at impact. So when we saw it rotate, it was not -- it is not a usual thing to happen. Somebody deliberately screwed and unscrewed the ring, and that is certain. And a great deal of force had to be applied to it, because if you'd brought in another one, you'd see how hard it is to have it rotate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well. And before we break, if you do have an opportunity during the break to check any of those calculations, and you will have an opportunity to make any corrections to my calculations after the break that you wish to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll adjourn for today and resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 22nd day of May, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.38 p.m.,
